MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE SCREAM & THEY DONT CARE - KIEL GERMANY 1997
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson played Kiel on the HIStory World Tour on Friday, June 13, 1997, at the Nordmarksportfeld in Kiel, Schleswig-Holstein. It was a sold-out second-leg show, listed at 55,000 of 55,000; local reporting put the crowd at more than 50,000.

It sat in the European restart of the tour, which had opened on May 31 in Bremen. The two shows immediately before Kiel were June 8 and June 10 at the Amsterdam Arena; the next stop was June 15 at Parkstadion in Gelsenkirchen. More than 50 trucks brought the stage into the field, and the date was treated locally as a one-off for the city. The Nordmarksportfeld has not hosted a concert on that scale since.

The show used the 1997 HIStory production: the “Great Gate of Kiev” tape opening and the rocket entrance, then the usual first block of “Scream,” “They Don’t Care About Us,” and “In the Closet,” followed by “Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’,” “Stranger in Moscow,” and “Smooth Criminal.” “The Way You Make Me Feel” was still in the set (it was dropped after Gelsenkirchen two days later). The Off the Wall medley was already gone, having been cut after Amsterdam on June 10. “Blood on the Dance Floor,” added for the second leg after the remix album, was in the show. The rest of the set ran through the Jackson 5 medley, “Billie Jean,” “Thriller,” “Beat It,” “Dangerous,” “Black or White,” “Earth Song,” “Heal the World,” and “HIStory.”

Crew accounts from the night describe fans throwing stuffed animals onto the stage and people being lifted over the barrier after fainting.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE BLACK OR WHITE SYDNEY 🇦🇺 1996
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson played Sydney twice on the HIStory World Tour, both nights at the Sydney Cricket Ground.

Thursday, 14 November 1996 and Saturday, 16 November 1996. These were the Australian opening dates, straight after two nights in Auckland (9 and 11 November) and before Brisbane on 19 November. Wikipedia’s tour table lists the Sydney stand as sold out, 86,000 across the two nights. A contemporary UPI report called the first night a sell-out and put that crowd at about 70,000.

The show used the 1996 HIStory set. The sequence reported for the 14 November concert was:
1. Scream / They Don’t Care About Us / In the Closet
2. Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’
3. Stranger in Moscow
4. Smooth Criminal
5. You Are Not Alone
6. The Way You Make Me Feel
7. Jackson 5 medley — I Want You Back / The Love You Save / I’ll Be There
8. Off the Wall medley — Rock with You / Off the Wall / Don’t Stop ’Til You Get Enough
9. Billie Jean
10. Thriller
11. Beat It
12. Dangerous
13. Black or White
14. Earth Song
15. Heal the World
16. HIStory

The night opened with the taped “Great Gates of Kiev” intro, with video interludes (“The Wind,” “Remember the Time,” the panther sequence, “We Are the World”) between songs. The 16 November show followed the same structure.
The Sydney stop is also when he married Debbie Rowe. On 14 November he announced he would marry her, a longtime friend who was pregnant, in a private ceremony. They married shortly after midnight on 15 November 1996 in his suite at the Sheraton-on-the-Park hotel, between the two concerts. He stayed largely out of sight otherwise, apart from outings to the zoo and a cinema, and asked the public to leave them alone.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE SCREAM - MOSCOW (HISTORY WORLD TOUR) 1996
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson played Moscow on the HIStory World Tour on Tuesday, September 17, 1996, at Dynamo Stadium (Stadion Dinamo). It was the fourth show of the tour, after Prague (September 7), Budapest (September 10), and Bucharest (September 14), and before Warsaw on September 20.

He arrived in Moscow on Sunday, September 15, at Vnukovo-II airport, where several hundred fans, mostly teenage girls, were let onto the apron. He left the plane in his usual black surgical mask, got into a police vehicle when the crowd pressed in, and stayed in the presidential suite at the Balchug Kempinski. About 45,000 tickets had been expected. Contemporary wire reports put the crowd at more than 40,000 to 45,000; tour listings usually give 50,000; later Russian accounts put it at about 71,000 and call it the biggest show Dynamo had hosted to that point.

The concert ran about two hours. He opened by rising out of a space-capsule prop to “The Great Gate of Kiev,” the standard first-leg HIStory opening. The set included “Scream,” “They Don’t Care About Us,” “In the Closet,” “Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’,” “Stranger in Moscow,” “Smooth Criminal,” “You Are Not Alone,” “The Way You Make Me Feel,” a Jackson 5 medley, an Off the Wall medley, “Billie Jean,” “Thriller,” “Beat It,” “Come Together,” “Dangerous,” “Black or White,” “Earth Song,” “Heal the World,” and “HIStory.”

The Russian promoter was ARS. This was his second Moscow concert. The first was the Dangerous World Tour at Luzhniki on September 15, 1993, played in heavy rain. The day after the 1996 show he was received at the Poklonnaya Gora war memorial by a military band.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON MEXICO DEPOSITION SNIPPET 1993
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson’s videotaped deposition in Mexico was taken in Mexico City on November 8 and November 10, 1993. It was not about the child-abuse allegations.

It was a civil copyright case in Los Angeles Superior Court. Songwriters, including Reynard (also spelled Rainard) Jones and Robert Smith, claimed Jackson had stolen “The Girl Is Mine,” “Thriller,” and “We Are the World.” Other defendants included Quincy Jones and Lionel Richie. Plaintiff’s counsel Howard Manning Jr. later said in a sworn declaration that he spent about 10 hours taking Jackson’s testimony across those two days. The circulating video is shorter: for years about three hours was known to exist, and a later copy runs about four hours, mostly from the November 10 session.
Reuters filmed him taking the oath and answering basic questions in Mexico City on those dates. He identified his occupation as “entertainer, dancer, singer, songwriter,” and denied the songs came from the plaintiffs.

Context and his condition:
* He was in Mexico for the Dangerous World Tour, with shows at Estadio Azteca, including November 7, 9, and 11. He canceled the rest of the tour on November 12 and left for treatment.
* He had recently had oral surgery (wisdom-tooth extraction) and was on painkillers. On tape he is drowsy, heavy-lidded, and slow to answer. He struggled with dates, album titles, and at points the names of the Jackson 5, and he hummed and beatboxed to explain how he wrote without reading music.
* Manning said he had been warned about the painkillers but saw no clear impairment, and that Jackson’s manner matched his 1989 deposition in the same case. Jackson’s own lawyer, Eve H. Wagner, said that on November 7 he was glassy-eyed, slurred, and barely able to stay awake from the medication, then improved.

The tape was played to jurors in mid-December 1993. Jackson did not give the Chandler civil deposition in Mexico. That was set for January 18, 1994; the case settled in January 1994 before it happened.

MICHAEL JACKSON MEETS PRINCESS DIANA WEMBLEY LONDON 1988
snippet.description:
These two legends met backstage at Wembley Stadium on Saturday, 16 July 1988, before the third of Michael Jackson’s seven sold-out Bad Tour shows there.

Diana, then Princess of Wales, and Prince Charles were among about 72,000 people at the show. Jackson met them before he went on. Contemporary reports and his own later account line up on the main points.
He handed over charity cheques from the Wembley run. Figures differ slightly by source: the Los Angeles Times the following Monday reported cheques of more than $400,000 for the Prince’s Trust and a children’s hospital; later accounts put it at about £150,000 for the Prince’s Trust and a further £100,000 for Great Ormond Street Hospital. His official account has described a $450,000 cheque for the Prince’s Trust. He also gave custom Bad tour jackets for the young princes William and Harry, and a framed commemorative disc.

The part people still talk about is “Dirty Diana.” Jackson had taken the song out of that night’s set because the title is about a groupie, not the princess, and he did not want to offend her. She pulled him aside and asked if he was going to do it. He said no, he had cut it because of her. She told him it was one of her favourites and to put it back in. He did. The official Live at Wembley July 16, 1988 release includes the song. What actually got dropped for time was “The Way You Make Me Feel,” because the royal meeting delayed the start.

Charles was reported to have asked Jackson if he could teach him to dance. Jackson later told Barbara Walters, in 1997, that Diana said she was honoured to meet him. It was their only face-to-face meeting. He said they stayed in touch afterwards by phone, often late at night.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE BLOOD ON THE DANCE-FLOOR COPENHAGEN 1997
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson performed in Copenhagen, Denmark, during the massive HIStory World Tour, bringing his signature theatrics to the city for two separate shows in the summer of 1997.
Here are the specific dates and details for his Copenhagen stops:

The Dates & Venue
Dates: August 14, 1997, and August 29, 1997
Venue: Parken Stadium, Copenhagen, Denmark

Tour Leg: The second leg of the HIStory World Tour (European summer run)
Concert Details & Highlights 

The 39th Birthday Surprise: The August 29th concert is a legendary piece of Michael Jackson history because it landed right on his 39th birthday. Following his performance of *You Are Not Alone*, Jackson was surprised on stage by a full marching band and a massive birthday cake. The entire stadium of Danish fans joined in to sing "Happy Birthday" to him, making it one of the most heartwarming, genuine moments of the entire tour.

Theatrics and Staging: The Copenhagen shows featured the massive, high-budget production elements the HIStory Tour was known for. This included his famous "rocket ship" entrance (emerging in a gold spacesuit), the intense military drill choreography for *They Don't Care About Us*, and the iconic anti-gravity lean during *Smooth Criminal*.

Archival Footage: While neither of the Copenhagen concerts received a standalone, official DVD release from Jackson's estate, the August 29th birthday show was professionally recorded. High-quality footage of this concert has been widely circulated and remastered by fans online over the years.

The Setlist
The concerts featured an incredible run of his biggest hits. The August 14th show uniquely featured Blood on the Dance Floor (which was swapped out of the setlist for later tour dates). 
A standard run of the songs performed in Copenhagen included:
 * **Medley:** *Scream* / *They Don't Care About Us* / *In the Closet*
 * *Wanna Be Startin' Somethin'*
 * *Stranger in Moscow*
 * *Smooth Criminal*
 * *You Are Not Alone*
 * **The Jackson 5 Medley:** *I Want You Back* / *The Love You Save* / *I'll Be There*
 * *Billie Jean*
 * *Thriller*
 * *Beat It*
 * *Blood on the Dance Floor* (August 14th show only)
 * *Dangerous*
 * *Black or White*
 * *Earth Song*
 * *Heal the World*
 * *HIStory*

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE BREMEN GERMANY JAM - DANGEROUS WORLD TOUR 1992
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson played one Dangerous World Tour show in Bremen: Saturday 8 August 1992 at the Weserstadion.

It was a single date, between Cardiff Arms Park on 5 August and Volksparkstadion in Hamburg on 10 August. Tour listings count it as the 17th concert of the tour. Wikipedia records attendance as 42,000 out of 42,000; some contemporary and fan accounts put the crowd closer to 45,000. Surviving recordings run about two hours.

The set was the standard early-leg Dangerous show:
* Carmina Burana “Brace Yourself” introduction
* Jam
* Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’
* Human Nature
* Smooth Criminal
* I Just Can’t Stop Loving You (with Siedah Garrett)
* She’s Out of My Life
* Jackson 5 medley (I Want You Back / The Love You Save / I’ll Be There)
* Thriller
* Billie Jean
* Black or White “panther” interlude
* Working Day and Night
* Beat It
* “Someone Put Your Hand Out” tape intro into Will You Be There
* Black or White
* “We Are the World” interlude
* Heal the World
* Man in the Mirror

A few production notes from the night stand out. The two-storey set piece was not used for Thriller or Heal the World, so the usual Thriller coffin illusion was dropped and replaced with a reprise of the choreography. Spark effects on several dancers failed at the end of Smooth Criminal. 

During the Heal the World ballet intro, dancer Michelle Berube dropped the globe. On Man in the Mirror the playback ran longer than on other dates before it cut.

Amateur and soundboard recordings of the full show circulate widely, and fans often rate the Bremen tape as one of the better-sounding leaked Dangerous Tour concerts.

snippet.title: MICHAEL JACKSON LIVE JAM & BLACK OR WHITE LONDON AUGUST 23rd 1992 - DANGEROUS WORLD TOUR
snippet.description:
Michael Jackson played five sold-out shows at Wembley Stadium on the Dangerous World Tour in 1992. A sixth date was cancelled at the last minute and rescheduled.

Dates

Date Status

Thursday 30 July 1992 Played
Friday 31 July 1992 Played
Saturday 1 August 1992 Cancelled about an hour before he was due on stage (viral infection / doctor-ordered bed rest). Rescheduled to 23 August; tickets remained valid, with refunds offered until 15 August.
Thursday 20 August 1992 Played (brought forward from the originally announced 21 August)
Saturday 22 August 1992 Played
Sunday 23 August 1992 Played (the makeup date for 1 August)

Wikipedia groups attendance as 144,000 for the two July nights and 216,000 for the three August nights — about 72,000 a night, which matches contemporary reports of a sell-out at the old Wembley Stadium.

Show details
Support acts included Kris Kross and Rozalla. Some listings also put TLC and D’Influence on the bill for the later dates. Support started around 6:15 pm; Jackson typically came on around 8 pm and played for roughly two to two and a half hours.

The staging opened with a Carmina Burana “Brace Yourself” intro, then Jackson rose through a trapdoor in a burst of gold glitter. A Los Angeles Times review of the 30 July show described a sell-out crowd of about 72,000 and a production built around trapdoors, choreography and a heavy mix of new Dangerous material with older hits.

Typical setlist:
* Jam
* Wanna Be Startin’ Somethin’
* Human Nature
* Smooth Criminal
* I Just Can’t Stop Loving You
* She’s Out of My Life
* Jackson 5 medley (I Want You Back / The Love You Save / I’ll Be There)
* Thriller
* Billie Jean
* Working Day and Night (after the “panther” interlude)
* Beat It
* Will You Be There (often after a “Someone Put Your Hand Out” tape intro)
* Black or White
* Heal the World
* Man in the Mirror

These London dates sat in the first European leg, which had opened in Munich on 27 June 1992. Other UK dates that summer were Cardiff Arms Park (5 August), Roundhay Park in Leeds (16 August) and Glasgow Green (18 August).
